title: Compatible unit changes of equations on full root towers
statement: Let $p$ be a positive prime, $H$ a commutative ring of characteristic $p$, and $r\geq0$. Let $t_i,t'_i\in H$, $a_i\in H^\times$ satisfy $t'_i=a_it_i$. Suppose units $b_{i,n}\in H^\times$ are given for every $n>0$ prime to $p$, with $b_{i,n}^n=a_i$ and $b_{i,m}^{m/n}=b_{i,n}$ for $n\mid m$. Form $H_n=H[x_{i,n}]/(x_{i,n}^n-t_i)$ and $H'_n=H[x'_{i,n}]/((x'_{i,n})^n-t'_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with power transitions. The assignments $x'_{i,n}\mapsto b_{i,n}x_{i,n}$ define coefficient-preserving isomorphisms $H'_n\to H_n$, commute with every divisibility transition, and induce isomorphisms on the full colimits and their localizations [def-weil-ring-localization-away] at $\prod_i t'_i$ and $\prod_i t_i$. They also respect reduction by the boundary ideals and commute with homomorphisms of all these coefficient and unit-root data. For a finite family $t^{(a)}_i=a^{(a)}_it_i$ with compatible roots $b^{(a)}_{i,n}$ of $a^{(a)}_i$, choose the roots of $a^{(a)}_i/a^{(b)}_i$ to be $b^{(a)}_{i,n}/b^{(b)}_{i,n}$. The resulting comparisons satisfy the identity and cocycle laws at finite, residual, full, and punctured levels. The case $r=0$ gives identity maps; the case $n=1$ is substitution of the original equations.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133, labelled parameter-root presentations; agent explicit substitution for unit changes, with coherent normalization against one reference equation.

proof.text: Write $N=\{n\in\mathbf N:n>0,\ (n,p)=1\}$ and $P_n=H[X_i]$, $I_n=(X_i^n-t_i)$, and similarly $P'_n,I'_n$. Polynomial evaluation gives $e_n:P'_n\to H_n$ fixing $H$ and sending $X'_i$ to $b_{i,n}x_{i,n}$. Each generator of $I'_n$ maps to $b_{i,n}^nt_i-t'_i=a_it_i-a_it_i=0$. Hence every sum of polynomial multiples of these generators maps to zero. Define $\phi_n([P])=e_n(P)$: if $[P]=[Q]$, then $P-Q\in I'_n$, so the two values agree. This gives a ring map $H'_n\to H_n$. Replacing $b_{i,n}$ by $b_{i,n}^{-1}$ gives $\psi_n:H_n\to H'_n$, since $(b_{i,n}^{-1}x'_{i,n})^n=b_{i,n}^{-n}t'_i=t_i$. Both composites fix coefficients and variables, so polynomial uniqueness followed by surjectivity of the quotient maps makes them identity maps.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: For $n\mid m$ put $q=m/n$. The transition $u_{nm}:H_n\to H_m$, $x_{i,n}\mapsto x_{i,m}^q$, is well defined because $(x_{i,m}^q)^n=t_i$; define $u'_{nm}$ similarly. Their identities and composition laws follow by multiplying exponents. On a primed generator the two sides of $u_{nm}\phi_n=\phi_m u'_{nm}$ are $b_{i,n}x_{i,m}^q$ and $(b_{i,m}x_{i,m})^q=b_{i,m}^qx_{i,m}^q$, equal by the assumed coherence. They agree on coefficients, and hence on every polynomial class. The inverse maps commute as well by the same equality for inverse units.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: The full compatible-root quotient is the colimit of the actual finite-stage power diagram. Given a cocone into a commutative H-algebra B, send each labelled generator x_(i,n) to the image of x_i under the n-th cocone component. Its power relation holds because that component is an H-algebra map; its divisibility relation holds by cocone naturality and the finite power-map formula. Polynomial evaluation therefore descends to the full quotient. It agrees with each cocone component by checking coefficients and variables. Any other factorization agrees on coefficients and on every labelled root by its finite-stage factorization, hence is equal by quotient and polynomial uniqueness. Direct evaluation x'_(i,n) to b_(i,n)x_(i,n) preserves both kinds of full relations by power and coherence of the units; inverse-unit evaluation is inverse, as at finite level. This gives the full comparison and its compatibility with every coprojection.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: Put $f=\prod_i t_i$, $f'=\prod_i t'_i$ and $A=\prod_i a_i\in H^\times$, so $f'=Af$. For $R=H_n$ or $H_\infty$ and its primed partner $R'$, the coefficient-preserving comparison $\phi$ sends $f'$ to $Af$, which is invertible in $R_f$ with inverse $A^{-1}f^{-1}$. The localization universal property therefore extends it uniquely to $R'_{f'}\to R_f$, with formula $z/(f')^k\mapsto\phi(z)A^{-k}/f^k$. The inverse comparison extends because it sends $f$ to $A^{-1}f'$. The composites restrict to identities on $R$ and $R'$, so localization uniqueness makes them identities. The same uniqueness applied to the finite-stage coprojections proves compatibility with the full localized comparison.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: For any subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ the comparison carries the ideal $(x'_{i,n}:i\in S)$ onto $(x_{i,n}:i\in S)$: its generators are multiplied by units, and its inverse divides by the same units. It also carries the coefficient boundary ideal $(t'_i:i\in S)$ onto $(t_i:i\in S)$ because $t'_i=a_it_i$. Thus $[z]\mapsto[\phi_n(z)]$ defines inverse maps on both sorts of boundary quotients: a difference in either ideal has image in its corresponding ideal. Power transitions preserve these ideals and their compatibility after reduction follows from the equality in step 2. At the full level the identical argument applies to the ideals generated by the coprojection images of these generators; step 3 proves compatibility with the finite reductions. Applying it to products of the boundary equations also gives their principal ideals. If reduction is followed by localization, the induced maps are the unique extensions of these quotient maps as in step 4, including a zero localized ring.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: Let $h:H\to K$ be a homomorphism preserving $t_i,t'_i,a_i$ and the specified $b_{i,n}$ (with the same $p,r$). Coefficient application and $x_{i,n}\mapsto y_{i,n}$ give maps of presented rings: the relations map to the defining relations over $K$. In the comparison square both composites on $x'_{i,n}$ equal $h(b_{i,n})y_{i,n}$, and on coefficients they equal $h$. Polynomial uniqueness and quotient surjectivity give equality. The inverse and power-transition squares follow by the same formulas. Boundary quotients retain the equality on classes; the full squares follow by precomposition with each coprojection and colimit uniqueness; the punctured squares follow by localization uniqueness, since $h(f)$ is the target boundary product. This proves naturality for every specified homomorphism of data.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: For the finite family, denote its level-$n$ algebra by $H_n^{(a)}$. Define $c_{ab,n}:H_n^{(a)}\to H_n^{(b)}$ by $x^{(a)}_{i,n}\mapsto (b^{(a)}_{i,n}/b^{(b)}_{i,n})x^{(b)}_{i,n}$. The ratio has $n$th power $a_i^{(a)}/a_i^{(b)}$ and obeys the power-transition coherence, so steps 1–4 apply. The identity ratio is $1$, and the composite $c_{bc,n}c_{ab,n}$ multiplies a generator by $(b^{(a)}_{i,n}/b^{(b)}_{i,n})(b^{(b)}_{i,n}/b^{(c)}_{i,n})=b^{(a)}_{i,n}/b^{(c)}_{i,n}$. Thus $c_{aa,n}=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_{bc,n}c_{ab,n}=c_{ac,n}$ by polynomial uniqueness and quotient surjectivity. Equality persists on residual classes, on full colimits by testing coprojections, and on punctures by localization uniqueness, giving every stated identity and cocycle law.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1, p.133: displayed parameter-root presentation; agent calculation of coordinate substitutions and their compatibilities.

proof.text: For r=0, polynomial induction shows that coefficients surject onto each finite stage and onto the full presented algebra, since there are no variables. Surjectivity remains after every boundary quotient. The root-coordinate and coefficient-equation ideals are zero; the principal ideal of the empty product is the unit ideal and gives the zero ring. The puncture element is one in every such quotient, so localization is again generated by coefficients, including in the zero ring. Each comparison fixes coefficients, giving the stated coefficient representative for every element. For n=1, the prescribed power identity gives b_(i,n)=a_i and the defining relation gives x_(i,n)=t_i. The comparison is thus b_(i,n)x_(i,n)=a_i t_i=t'_i.
